why: MI-217, the consumer half of the operator-approved producer-first plan (MI-216 landed as 456680bb8). The M7 daily strategy-review gate withheld every verdict for want of live in-window closes and called it `hold` -- 52 of 52 legs on eight consecutive days -- which the promotion-evidence doctrine forbids (edge is proven OFFLINE, live rows prove MECHANICS; clause 3 bars any gate requiring calendar-time accrual to prove edge). This makes the ABSENCE legible: where the gate would say `hold` for want of live closes AND no offline record exists, it now says `no_offline_evidence`. Adds scripts/ml/_offline_evidence.py (a reader that IMPORTS the producer's vocabulary rather than copying it), wires it through decide(), publishes the state on the packet and the INDEX, and adds its own summary count. NO threshold moved, NO KILL/DEMOTE path altered, no leg retired, nothing routed to the sunset pass. `offline=None` is byte-for-byte the old behaviour and a test pins it.
hold_text: The diff touches `scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py`, which is OUTSIDE TIER1_SURFACE (that allowlist carries scripts/ci, scripts/ops, scripts/research, scripts/reports -- not scripts/ml). Per R5 this cannot self-land and wants a human read, which is right: it is the M7 VERDICT function. Thank you to MI-226 (#11592) for adding this hold_reason hours ago -- before it existed the only available values overstated the tier, which is what BL-20260909-PR-LANDING-HOLD-REASONS-HAS-NO-VALUE-FOR-TIER-1-ON-AN-UNCERTIFIABLE-PATH was filed about. ⚠️ ONE DESIGN DECISION A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK RATHER THAN TAKE ON TRUST: `is_actionable` was `action != "hold"`, so ANY new verdict counted as actionable. Left alone, `no_offline_evidence` would have flipped ~54 of 55 legs to `actionable: true` on day one and buried the rows that genuinely ask the operator for a decision. I made it non-actionable via an explicit NON_DECISION_VERDICTS set -- but the OPPOSITE error is worse, so it is NOT silent: it rides `by_action`, gets its own `no_offline_evidence` summary count, and a per-state census. Quiet, never invisible. Both failure directions are pinned by tests with planted-defect positive controls (reverting either fix fails them). ⚠️ AND THE RATCHET DID NOT MOVE, DELIBERATELY: soak-doctrine still reports 7 accrual-gated branches in this file, because they still key on n_closed -- this change makes the absence visible, it does not remove the accrual gate. Lowering that count is the larger Tier-3 change of sourcing the EDGE verdict from the offline record, which is NOT what was approved. The ledger now records that in `narrowed_note` so no future session reads the unchanged 7 as this change having failed.
